frequency_question: What is the historical success rate of finalizing and notifying complex financial incentive schemes within a compressed administrative window?
membership_rule: Includes all major central-level automotive/manufacturing transition subsidy and credit guarantee policies proposed by the Ministry of Heavy Industries since 2015. Excludes routine budgetary allocations or minor amendments.

cases.name: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Auto & Auto Components

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 major named schemes; represents the universe of primary automotive and EV transition financial schemes launched by the Ministry in this timeframe.
known_gaps: Minor sub-schemes or delayed pilot programs that did not reach full formal gazette notification stage are omitted from the primary policy class.
skeleton: Total major sector-specific incentive/subsidy schemes introduced and successfully notified by the Ministry of Heavy Industries relative to those formally proposed for cabinet/inter-ministerial clearance in the last decade.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 5 major proposed schemes passing through standard bureaucratic friction channels.
validity_reason: Bureaucratic clearance norms and standard operating procedures for central industrial subsidies remain stable across current administrative frameworks.
